topic: the 1835 Great Moon Hoax -- a New York newspaper's fake bat-people-on-the-moon story fooled Yale scientists and briefly made it the best-selling paper on Earth
title: The 1835 Newspaper Hoax That Convinced America the Moon Had Bat-People
description: AI-narrated commentary on the 1835 Great Moon Hoax: how a New York newspaper convinced readers the moon was home to bat-winged humanoids and blue unicorns, fooled a team of Yale scientists sent to verify it, and briefly became the best-selling newspaper on Earth. Original commentary, not a reproduction of any source video.

hook_candidates.text: The 1835 newspaper hoax that convinced half of America there were bat-people living on the moon.
What if one newspaper convinced an entire country that bat-people lived on the moon, and nobody was ever punished for it?
You think fake news is new? In 1835 a newspaper invented an entire moon civilization and got away with it.
In August 1835, a New York newspaper announced astronomers had discovered bat-winged men living on the moon.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists 'fake news' only started with the internet, because they want to watch them lose it over bat-people on the moon in 1835.
contradicted_belief: Most people think 'fake news' about bat-people on the moon is a modern internet invention, not something an 1835 newspaper hoax already pulled off.
closing_comment: Wildest part of this 1835 newspaper hoax: the real astronomer never even sued over the fake bat-people on the moon.
